title: Constitution of the FRN 1999 (as amended) — s.35 Right to Personal Liberty
text: Every person is entitled to personal liberty and no person shall be deprived of his liberty except in defined circumstances, such as execution of a court sentence or reasonable suspicion of having committed an offence, and even then subject to conditions. Any person who is arrested or detained shall have the right to remain silent or avoid answering any question until after consultation with a legal practitioner or any other person of his own choice. The person arrested must be informed within twenty-four hours (or such other period as a court considers reasonable in the circumstances) of the facts and grounds of his arrest. Any person who is unlawfully arrested or detained shall be entitled to compensation and public apology from the appropriate authority or person.

title: Constitution 1999 — s.34 Right to Dignity of the Human Person
text: Every individual is entitled to respect for the dignity of his person, and accordingly no person shall be subjected to torture or to inhuman or degrading treatment; no person shall be held in slavery or servitude; and no person shall be required to perform forced or compulsory labour.

title: Constitution 1999 — s.36 Right to Fair Hearing
text: In the determination of his civil rights and obligations, including any question or determination by or against any government or authority, a person shall be entitled to a fair hearing within a reasonable time by a court or other tribunal established by law and constituted in such manner as to secure its independence and impartiality. Every person who is charged with a criminal offence shall be presumed innocent until he is proved guilty.

title: Constitution 1999 — s.37 Right to Private and Family Life
text: The privacy of citizens, their homes, correspondence, telephone conversations and telegraphic communications is hereby guaranteed and protected.

title: Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015 — s.6 Humane Treatment of Suspects
text: A suspect shall be accorded humane treatment, having regard to his right to dignity of the human person, and shall not be subjected to torture, cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment. A suspect shall not be arrested in place of a suspect who is not available. A suspect shall not be subjected to restraining techniques or equipment except as reasonably necessary, and restraints shall be removed when no longer necessary.

title: Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015 — s.8 Recording of Arrest and Obligations of Arresting Officer
text: The Police officer or other person making the arrest shall, at the time of arrest, inform the suspect of the reason for the arrest. The police officer making an arrest shall record in a prescribed form the fact of the arrest, the reason, the date and time, and the station where the suspect is detained. Where a suspect is arrested without a warrant, the police shall promptly inform a superior officer and a legal practitioner may apply for the suspect to be released.

title: Police Act 2020 — Duties of the Police and Arrest Powers
text: The police have the duty to protect life and property, preserve law and order, and prevent and detect crime. An arrest must be made strictly in accordance with the law; unnecessary restraint is prohibited; and an arrested person must be brought before a court within a reasonable time. The Act strengthens accountability mechanisms including the Complaints Response Unit for public complaints against police officers.

title: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 — Data Subject Rights and NDPC Complaints
section: Part on data subject rights; s.40
text: A data subject has rights including the right to be informed, right of access to personal data, right to rectification, right to erasure, right to data portability, and the right to object to processing including direct marketing. A data controller must process personal data lawfully and protect it; personal data breaches must be notified to the Commission within 72 hours where there is a risk of harm. A data subject who is aggrieved by the conduct of a data controller or data processor may lodge a complaint with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC), which can investigate and issue enforcement notices and administrative fines.

title: Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act 2015 (amended 2024)
text: Key offences include: system interference and unauthorized access to computer systems; identity theft and impersonation; cyberstalking and online harassment including threats communicated through computer; and phishing. Knowingly transmitting communication that is false or created to bully, threaten or harass another person, or transmitting intimate images to coerce or harass, attracts criminal liability. Complaints may be made to the police and to the relevant cybercrime units.

title: Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act 2015
text: Prohibits all forms of violence against persons in private and public life, including physical, sexual, psychological, verbal and economic abuse, intimidation and harassment, including against spouses and intimate partners. It establishes offences such as rape, coercion, and intentional emotional or psychological abuse, provides for protection orders, and mandates support for survivors including access to shelters and medical assistance. The Act applies in the FCT and has been domesticated by many states.

title: Legal Aid Act 2011 — Legal Aid Council of Nigeria
text: Establishes the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria to provide free legal assistance to indigent persons — those who cannot afford legal representation — in criminal and civil matters including pre-trial detention, bail, and certain civil cases. Eligible persons include persons in custody who cannot afford a lawyer, children in conflict with the law, and persons with insufficient means. Services include legal advice, representation in court, and assistance with alternative dispute resolution.

title: National Human Rights Commission Act (1995, amended 2010)
text: Establishes the National Human Rights Commission with the mandate to deal with all matters relating to the protection of human rights guaranteed by the Constitution, treaties and laws. The Commission can receive complaints of human rights violations, investigate them, mediate, and in some cases refer matters to the Attorney-General for prosecution. It covers violations by public officials including law enforcement.

title: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018
text: Establishes the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) as the apex consumer protection body. It prohibits false, misleading or deceptive representations, regulates consumer agreements, and gives consumers rights against unfair, unreasonable and unjust contract terms and practices. Consumers may lodge complaints with the FCCPC which can investigate and compel remedies.

title: Lagos State Tenancy Law 2011
text: Governs tenancy relationships in Lagos State. A landlord may only recover possession of premises through due process: valid notice to quit as prescribed by the tenancy type, and an order of court obtained through due process. Self-help eviction — including forcible entry, removing roofs or doors, or harassing a tenant out — is unlawful. Rent increases and receipts are regulated.
